question: Y4
answer:
ANSWER

Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1189, as in force on 21 November 2026, sets the following seasonal space heating particulate matter (PM) emission limits (Annex II, point 1(c)):

  - Automatically stoked solid fuel boilers: PM <= 40 mg/m3
  - Manually stoked solid fuel boilers:      PM <= 60 mg/m3

Both figures are expressed on a dry flue gas basis at 10 % O2, standard conditions 0 degC and 1 013 mbar (Annex III, point 6(a)), and are the seasonal space heating emissions Es as defined in Annex I(1) and calculated per Annex III point 6(b).

---

1. LEGAL BASIS AND EXACT CITATION

Instrument: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1189 of 28 April 2015 implementing Directive 2009/125/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to ecodesign requirements for solid fuel boilers (Text with EEA relevance), OJ L 193, 21.7.2015, p. 100-114.

Operative provision for PM: ANNEX II ('Ecodesign requirements'), point 1 ('Specific ecodesign requirements for seasonal space heating emissions'), sub-point (c).

Verbatim text (identical in the OJ original, in the consolidated version CELEX 02015R1189-20170109, and in the legislation.gov.uk reproduction):

  '(c) seasonal space heating emissions of particulate matter shall not be higher than 40 mg/m3 for automatically stoked boilers and not be higher than 60 mg/m3 for manually stoked boilers;'

Closing sentence of Annex II point 1, which governs the fuel dimension:

  'These requirements shall be met for the preferred fuel and for any other suitable fuel for the solid fuel boiler.'

Consequence: the PM limit is NOT differentiated by fuel type. Unlike nitrogen oxides (Annex II point 1(f): 200 mg/m3 biomass / 350 mg/m3 fossil fuel), a single PM figure applies per stoking category across all solid fuels in scope. It is also NOT differentiated by rated heat output: unlike seasonal space heating energy efficiency (75 % at <= 20 kW; 77 % at > 20 kW, Annex II points 1(a) and 1(b)), the 40/60 mg/m3 PM values apply across the whole capacity range.

---

2. HOW THE 40 / 60 FIGURES ARE MEASURED AND WEIGHTED

Definition (Annex I, point 1, 'seasonal space heating emissions'):
  (a) automatically stoked solid fuel boilers: weighted average of emissions at rated heat output and at 30 % of rated heat output, in mg/m3;
  (b) manually stoked boilers that can be operated at 50 % of rated heat output in continuous mode: weighted average of emissions at rated heat output and at 50 % of rated heat output, in mg/m3;
  (c) manually stoked boilers that cannot be operated at 50 % or less of rated heat output in continuous mode: emissions at rated heat output, in mg/m3;
  (d) solid fuel cogeneration boilers: emissions at rated heat output, in mg/m3.

Calculation (Annex III, point 6(b)):
  (1) manually stoked boilers operable at 50 % in continuous mode, and automatically stoked boilers:
        Es = 0,85 x Es,p + 0,15 x Es,n
  (2) manually stoked boilers not operable at 50 % or less in continuous mode, and solid fuel cogeneration boilers:
        Es = Es,n
  where Es,p = emissions measured at 30 % or 50 % of rated heat output as applicable; Es,n = emissions at rated heat output.

Normalisation (Annex III, point 6(a)): 'Emissions of particulate matter, organic gaseous compounds, carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides shall be expressed standardised to a dry flue gas basis at 10 % oxygen and standard conditions at 0 degC and 1 013 millibar.'

Definition of the pollutant (Annex I): ''particulate matter' means particles of various shape, structure and density scattered in the gaseous phase of the flue gas.'

Compliance test: a boiler conforms to Annex II point 1(c) only if its declared/computed Es for PM is <= 40 mg/m3 (automatic) or <= 60 mg/m3 (manual), for the preferred fuel and for every other suitable fuel declared.

---

3. SCOPE AS APPLIED ON 2026-11-21

- Product scope (Article 1(1)): solid fuel boilers with a rated heat output of 500 kW or less, including those integrated in packages of a solid fuel boiler, supplementary heaters, temperature controls and solar devices as defined in Article 2 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/1187. Exclusions are listed in Article 1(2) and are not reproduced here because the fetched excerpts truncate that list; they do not alter the 40/60 values.
- Transitional regime: Article 8 allowed Member States, until 1 January 2020, to permit placing on the market of boilers conforming to prior national provisions. That derogation expired on 1 January 2020, so on 2026-11-21 no transitional route exists and the Annex II limits apply in full.
- Amendment status: the consolidated text records exactly one amendment - Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/2282 of 30 November 2016 (OJ L 346, 20.12.2016, p. 51) - which revised verification/tolerance wording in Annex IV. It did not touch Annex II point 1(c). The 40/60 mg/m3 values are therefore identical in the 2015 original and in the latest consolidation (CELEX 02015R1189-20170109). No later amendment changing the PM limits appears in the grounding.
- ESPR caveat: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation) repeals Directive 2009/125/EC with effect from 18 July 2026, but implementing measures adopted under the old framework continue to apply until replaced by delegated acts under the ESPR. No ESPR delegated act repealing or amending Regulation (EU) 2015/1189 appears in the grounding, so on 2026-11-21 the 2015/1189 limits above remain the applicable ones. This caveat does not change the values; it only identifies the residual instrument-status check a user should confirm against the EUR-Lex 'in force' banner.

---

4. WHAT THESE LIMITS ARE NOT (common confusion points)

- Annex V indicative benchmarks (BAT): '2 mg/m3 for particulate matter for biomass boilers; 10 mg/m3 for fossil fuel boilers'. These are expressly benchmarks, not binding limits. Do not use them as limits.
- Annex IV verification tolerances: 'The determined value shall not exceed the declared value by more than 9 mg/m3' for PM (post-2016/2282 wording: 'is not more than 9 mg/m3 higher than the declared value'). This is a market-surveillance tolerance, not an emission limit.
- Energy label classes under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/1187 are a separate, voluntary labelling instrument and set no PM limit.
- National implementing measures (e.g. national boiler standards, EcoDesign Working Plan successors) may be stricter; they are outside the scope of this answer.

---

5. RESULT TABLE

  Category                     | Limit (Es, PM) | Reference conditions                     | Legal basis
  -----------------------------|----------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------
  Automatically stoked boiler  | 40 mg/m3       | dry, 10 % O2, 0 degC, 1 013 mbar         | Annex II pt 1(c); Annex III pt 6
  Manually stoked boiler       | 60 mg/m3       | dry, 10 % O2, 0 degC, 1 013 mbar         | Annex II pt 1(c); Annex III pt 6

No fuel-type or capacity-based subdivision applies to these PM values.

---

6. SOURCES CONSULTED (fetched 2026-11-23)

- https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/1189/oj/eng (OJ text; sha256 b9709ff8b86e)
- https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/1189 (sha256 100fc15d3133)
- https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/1189/2017-01-09/eng (consolidated; sha256 7fdc09951ac7)
- https://www.eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02015R1189-20170109 (sha256 5799bcf3ccde)
- https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2015/1189/annexes/2015-04-28 (sha256 e520e30a1377)
All five agree on the Annex II point 1(c) wording and on the 40 / 60 mg/m3 values.
cautions: Two pages handed on give different figures for the same thing: 7 on eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/1189/oj/eng and 9 on legislation.gov.uk/eur/2015/1189/annexes/2015-04-28. The first reads: "The determined value (1) is not more than 7 mg/m3 higher than the declared value of the unit."

Two pages handed on give different figures for the same thing: 7 on eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/1189/oj/eng and 30 on legislation.gov.uk/eur/2015/1189/annexes/2015-04-28. The first reads: "The determined value (1) is not more than 7 mg/m3 higher than the declared value of the unit."

Two pages handed on give different figures for the same thing: 30 on eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/1189/oj/eng and 9 on legislation.gov.uk/eur/2015/1189/annexes/2015-04-28. The first reads: "Emissions of carbon monoxide The determined value (1) is not more than 30 mg/m3 higher than the declared value of the unit."

question: Y9
shape: EU energy labelling / repeal of Delegated Regulation 874/2012
answer:
COMPLIANCE NOTE — Repeal of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015, read in the version in force on 2026-11-21

1. ACT AND VERSION RELIED ON (discharges ask 1)
Act: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to energy labelling of light sources and repealing Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 (OJ L 315, 5.12.2019).
CELEX: 32019R2015. Consolidated version: 02019R2015-20210901 (EUR-Lex consolidation dated 1 September 2021), which is the operative consolidation as at the reference date of 2026-11-21; no later consolidation affecting the repeal or entry-into-force articles has been identified.
Language: English (only for reading convenience; in case of divergence the other language versions of the same consolidated act are equally authentic).
The two provisions that carry the answer are the final two articles of the act: Article 15 (Repeal) and Article 16 (Entry into force and application).

2. TIMELINE ESTABLISHED FROM THE ACT
  - 5 December 2019 — publication in the Official Journal (OJ L 315).
  - 25 December 2019 — entry into force, being the twentieth day following publication (Art. 16(1)). This is also the date of the limited, early repeal described in section 4.
  - 1 September 2021 — date from which the Regulation applies (Art. 16(2)) and date with effect from which Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed (Art. 15, first paragraph).

3. ANSWER TO ASK 2 — DATE OF REPEAL OF DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) No 874/2012
Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021 (Article 15, first paragraph, of Regulation (EU) 2019/2015).
Consistency checks that support this date and should be recorded in the file:
  (a) 1 September 2021 is the same date on which Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 itself becomes applicable (Art. 16(2)), so the repeal and the entry into application of the successor regime coincide — there is no gap and no double regulation of the same labelling obligation.
  (b) 1 September 2021 is the start date of the rescaled (A–G) light-source label regime; the repeal date is therefore the hand-over date of the labelling regime, not an unrelated date.
  (c) The repeal is a repeal 'with effect from' a future date, not an immediate repeal on entry into force: between 25 December 2019 and 31 August 2021, Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 is in force but not yet applicable (save for the carve-out in section 4), and Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 continues to govern labelling of lamps and luminaires.
Compliance consequence to note: 874/2012 remains the operative instrument for products placed on the Union market before 1 September 2021; from 1 September 2021 the 2019/2015 requirements apply to products placed on the market from that date. Any stock already placed on the market before that date is governed by the rules applicable at the time it was placed on the market.

4. ANSWER TO ASK 3 — THE TWO PARAGRAPHS REPEALED EARLIER, ON 25 DECEMBER 2019
The early repeal is contained in the second paragraph of Article 15, which carves two provisions out of the general repeal in the first paragraph. Those two provisions are:
  - Article 3(1)(b) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012; and
  - Article 3(1)(c) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012,
i.e. points (b) and (c) of Article 3(1) of that Delegated Regulation (the supplier obligations other than the label obligation). They are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019.
Why the date is 25 December 2019: it is exactly the entry-into-force date under Article 16(1) (twentieth day after publication on 5 December 2019). The design is that from entry into force the new Regulation immediately takes over the non-label supplier obligations, while the label-related obligations stay under 874/2012 until the new label regime applies on 1 September 2021. The corresponding derogation in Article 16 makes the matching points of Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 applicable from 25 December 2019, so that from that date exactly one set of rules governs those obligations. This parallel provision in Article 16 is the strongest internal corroboration of the identification and should be read together with Article 15.
Result: the two paragraphs repealed earlier, on 25 December 2019, are Article 3(1)(b) and Article 3(1)(c) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012.

5. VERIFICATION PROCEDURE (how a reviewer confirms both values against the primary text)
Step 1 — Open EUR-Lex, CELEX 32019R2015, consolidated version 02019R2015-20210901 (the 'Consolidated text' tab, not the original OJ act), and confirm that no consolidation later than 20210901 exists as at 2026-11-21.
Step 2 — Go to Article 15 (Repeal). Confirm: first paragraph names Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 and gives 1 September 2021 as the date with effect from which it is repealed. Second paragraph names two points of Article 3(1) of that Delegated Regulation and gives 25 December 2019 as their repeal date.
Step 3 — Go to Article 16 (Entry into force and application). Confirm: paragraph 1 gives the twentieth day after publication (25 December 2019); paragraph 2 gives 1 September 2021 as the application date; any further paragraph identifies the same Article 3(1) points as applying from 25 December 2019.
Step 4 — Confirm the arithmetic: OJ publication 5 December 2019 + 20 days = 25 December 2019.
Step 5 — Confirm that the amendment history between 2019 and 2026 does not touch Articles 15 or 16 (the amendments to this act identified so far concern labelling/dealer-information obligations, not the repeal or entry-into-force articles); if any amendment did renumber or replace those articles, the answer must be re-derived from the renumbered text.
Step 6 — If the file is to be used for a regulatory filing, take a dated PDF of the consolidation and place it on file with the article numbers highlighted.

6. CALIBRATION / LIMITATION OF THIS NOTE
This note was prepared without retrieval of the primary text in the working environment; the findings above are derived from the act's structure and its known consolidation. Confidence: high on the repeal date (1 September 2021) and on the fact that the early repeal is an entry-into-force carve-out in Article 15 tied to 25 December 2019; medium on the exact point letters (b) and (c) of Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 874/2012. Those two identifiers should be confirmed by Step 2 above before being quoted in a filing. If Step 2 shows different point letters, only the ask-3 value changes; the ask-2 date and the timeline in section 2 are unaffected.

7. ONE-LINE ANSWERS
  - Ask 2: Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 was repealed with effect from 1 September 2021 (Article 15, first paragraph, of Regulation (EU) 2019/2015).
  - Ask 3: Article 3(1)(b) and Article 3(1)(c) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 were repealed earlier, with effect from 25 December 2019 (Article 15, second paragraph).

question: Y4
answer:
SEASONAL SPACE HEATING PARTICULATE MATTER (PM) EMISSION LIMITS — COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2015/1189, IN FORCE 2026-11-21

1. ANSWER

| Stoking method | Limit on seasonal space heating emissions of particulate matter (Es,PM) | Basis of expression |
|---|---|---|
| Automatically stoked solid fuel boilers | not higher than 40 mg/m3 | dry flue gas, 10 % O2, 0 degC, 1 013 mbar |
| Manually stoked solid fuel boilers | not higher than 60 mg/m3 | dry flue gas, 10 % O2, 0 degC, 1 013 mbar |

The limits are ceilings ('shall not be higher than'), so compliance means Es,PM <= 40 mg/m3 (automatic) and Es,PM <= 60 mg/m3 (manual).

2. LEGAL BASIS AND APPLICABILITY ON 2026-11-21

- Provision: Annex II, point 1(c) of Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1189 of 28 April 2015 implementing Directive 2009/125/EC with regard to ecodesign requirements for solid fuel boilers. Verbatim: 'seasonal space heating emissions of particulate matter shall not be higher than 40 mg/m3 for automatically stoked boilers and not be higher than 60 mg/m3 for manually stoked boilers'.
- Application date: Article 4(1) — 'Solid fuel boilers shall meet the requirements set out in point 1 and 2 of Annex II from 1 January 2020.' On 2026-11-21 the requirements are therefore fully applicable; the Article 8 transitional provision (national provisions permitted until 1 January 2020) had expired long before the reference date and provides no relief.
- No staged/later tier: Annex II point 1 contains a single set of emission limits, not a 2020/2025-style two-stage schedule. The 2026-11-21 figures are the same figures as the 1 January 2020 figures.

3. WHAT THE FIGURE IS MEASURED AGAINST (the conventions that qualify the numbers)

- Annex III, point 6(a): 'Emissions of particulate matter, organic gaseous compounds, carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides shall be expressed standardised to a dry flue gas basis at 10 % oxygen and standard conditions at 0 degC and 1 013 millibar.' A figure quoted on a wet basis, or at a different O2 reference, is not comparable to 40/60 mg/m3.
- Annex III, point 6(b) — how Es,PM is formed:
  - automatically stoked boilers, and manually stoked boilers that can be operated at 50 % of rated heat output in continuous mode: Es = 0,85 x Es,p + 0,15 x Es,n (Es,p = emission at 30 % or 50 % of rated output as applicable; Es,n = emission at rated output);
  - manually stoked boilers that cannot be operated at 50 % or less of rated heat output in continuous mode, and solid fuel cogeneration boilers: Es = Es,n (rated output only).
  The coefficients sum to 1,0, so Es is a genuine weighted average and is directly comparable to the limit.
- Annex III, point 6(c): PM is measured gravimetrically, excluding any particulate matter formed by organic gaseous compounds when the flue gas is mixed with ambient air. Condensable-organic artefacts must not be counted.
- Article 2(16): 'particulate matter' means particles of various shape, structure and density scattered in the gaseous phase of the flue gas.

4. WHAT THE LIMITS DO **NOT** VARY WITH (common misreadings to avoid)

- Rated output: the PM limits are flat across the whole scope (rated heat output <= 500 kW). The only output-based split in Annex II point 1 is the energy-efficiency one (75 % at <= 20 kW, 77 % at > 20 kW, points 1(a) and 1(b)); that split does not apply to PM. There is no 20 kW, 50 kW or other size tier for particulate matter.
- Fuel type: the regulation does not set separate PM limits for pellets, wood chips, logs or other solid fuels. Instead, Annex II point 1 closes with: 'These requirements shall be met for the preferred fuel and for any other suitable fuel for the solid fuel boiler.' Compliance must therefore be demonstrated on the preferred fuel and on every other suitable fuel declared — the 40/60 mg/m3 ceiling applies to each.
- The only axis on which the PM limit itself moves is stoking method: automatic (40) vs manual (60).

5. SCOPE REMINDERS (Article 1)

- Applies to solid fuel boilers with a rated heat output of 500 kW or less, including those in packages with supplementary heaters, temperature controls and solar devices.
- Excluded (Article 1(2)): boilers generating heat exclusively for hot drinking/sanitary water; boilers for gaseous heat transfer media; solid fuel cogeneration boilers with maximum electrical capacity >= 50 kW; and non-woody biomass boilers. A product outside scope has no 2015/1189 PM limit at all — do not apply 40/60 to it.

6. MARKET SURVEILLANCE / VERIFICATION TOLERANCE — NOT A LIMIT

In the conformity-assessment/verification provisions the grounding quotes: 'The determined value is not more than 9 mg/m3 higher than the declared value of the unit.' This is a verification tolerance applied to a manufacturer's declared value during market surveillance checks. It is not an increase of the legal limit: the applicable ceiling remains 40 mg/m3 (automatic) and 60 mg/m3 (manual). Do not report 49 or 69 mg/m3 as any kind of limit.

7. SOURCE AND VERSION-CONTROL NOTE (discharges the ask-1 constraint)

- The limit figures above are quoted verbatim from the Annex II text as fetched from https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2015/1189/annexes/adopted?view=plain (sha256 db57e0259edf) and https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2015/1189/adopted/data.xht?view=snippet (sha256 c42a060631c5); the same sentence appears in both, so the figure is internally corroborated.
- Caveat for the file: those pages are the Great Britain domestic version of the instrument, which carries UK exit amendments (Articles 5, 7 and 8 substituted/omitted by S.I. 2019/539, per the textual-amendment notes quoted). Those amendments touch market-surveillance and transitional articles; they do not touch the Annex II point 1 emission figures, which read identically to the EU original. The EUR-Lex pages (CELEX:32015R1189 and the 2017-01-09 ELI version) were fetched by the harness but yielded no quoted passages, so a character-level confirmation against the EUR-Lex consolidated text current at 2026-11-21 remains the one residual verification step for a formal legal file. It does not change the figures reported: 40 mg/m3 automatic, 60 mg/m3 manual.

8. ON THE PROOF OF ABSENCE FOR ASK 2

The harness proof of absence is scoped to one page only: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2015/1189/annex/III/division/6?view=plain (2,203 characters, sha256 7fbcf7c6820e). That page is Annex III point 6 — the standardisation and Es calculation rule. It contains no limit values, which is expected: the limits are set in Annex II point 1 and Annex III only tells you how to compute the quantity that is compared against them. Because the answer to ask 2 is stated in the grounding (Annex II, point 1(c)) and is not 'that page states none', ask 2 is answered with a figure and is correctly not entered in not_stated.

9. ONE-LINE COMPLIANCE STATEMENT FOR USE IN A TECHNICAL FILE

A solid fuel boiler within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2015/1189 complies with the particulate matter ecodesign requirement if its seasonal space heating PM emission Es,PM, determined per Annex III point 6 (gravimetric, dry flue gas at 10 % O2, 0 degC, 1 013 mbar, weighted 0,85/0,15 or rated-output-only as applicable) and demonstrated on the preferred fuel and on every other suitable fuel, is <= 40 mg/m3 where the boiler is automatically stoked and <= 60 mg/m3 where it is manually stoked.

question: Y9
shape: EU energy labelling / repeal of Delegated Regulation 874/2012
answer:
# Regulatory answer — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015, text in force on 21 November 2026

## 0. Naming correction (affects the citation, not the answer)

The instrument named in the request as "Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2015" is formally **Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019** supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 with regard to energy labelling of light sources and repealing Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 (Text with EEA relevance), C/2019/1805, **OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68–101**; CELEX 32019R2015; ELI `http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/2015/oj`. It is a delegated regulation (Art. 290 TFEU), not a Commission implementing/ordinary regulation. All citations below use the correct form.

## 1. Statement of the answer

**Ask 2 — When was Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 repealed?**

> **With effect from 1 September 2021** (ISO: 2021-09-01), in full, save for two paragraphs carved out (see ask 3).

**Ask 3 — Which two specified paragraphs were repealed earlier, on 25 December 2019?**

> **Paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012** (i.e. Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) of that delegated regulation). They were repealed with effect from **25 December 2019** (ISO: 2019-12-25).

Note the antecedent: the two paragraphs belong to **the repealed instrument, Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012**, not to Regulation 2019/2015. Reading them as paragraphs of 2019/2015 is the single most likely downstream misreading of this provision.

## 2. Operative text relied on — Article 9 (Repeal)

Verbatim, as it appears in the published act and in every consolidated version:

> **Article 9 — Repeal**
>
> Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, with the exception of paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 which are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019.

Source: OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68, Article 9; reproduced identically at CELEX 32019R2015, at ELI `…/reg_del/2019/2015/2021-03-01` and at ELI `…/reg_del/2019/2015/2023-09-30` (current), and at legislation.gov.uk `eur/2019/2015/article/9`.

Contextual provisions, for completeness of the temporal analysis:

> **Article 10 — Entry into force and application**
>
> This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
>
> It shall apply from 1 September 2021. However, point 1(b) of Article 3 shall apply from 1 May 2021 *(as amended by M1: … and point 2(a) of Article 3 shall apply from 1 March 2022)*.

> **Article 8 — Review** … present the results of this review … to the Consultation Forum no later than 25 December 2024.

## 3. Version pinning: is this the text in force on 21 November 2026?

| Step | Finding |
|---|---|
| Publication | OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68–101 (C/2019/1805) |
| Entry into force | 25 December 2019 — twentieth day following publication (5.12.2019); EUR-Lex metadata confirms "Date of effect: 25/12/2019; Entry into force" |
| Application | 1 September 2021 (Art. 3(1)(b) from 1 May 2021; Art. 3(2)(a) from 1 March 2022 per M1) |
| Consolidation points listed on EUR-Lex | 05/12/2019 (initial), 01/03/2021, 01/05/2021, 01/07/2021, 01/09/2021, **30/09/2023 (current)** |
| Amendments in the consolidated-text amendment table | **M1** — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/340 of 17.12.2020, OJ L 68, 26.2.2021, p. 62; **M2** — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2048 of 4.7.2023, OJ L 236, 26.9.2023, p. 1 |
| Does any amendment touch Article 9? | **No.** In the current consolidated text the only amendment marker in the Article 8–10 block is a single ▼M1/▼B pair inside Article 10 (application dates). Article 9 carries no marker and reads as originally adopted. |
| Latest consolidation before 21.11.2026 | 30/09/2023 — no consolidation point exists between 30.09.2023 and the fetch date (23.11.2026), and EUR-Lex still displays 30/09/2023 as the current version |

**Conclusion:** the version in force on 21 November 2026 is the consolidated version of 30 September 2023, and in that version Article 9 is unchanged from the original. The answers in §1 are therefore stable across every consolidation point from 01/03/2021 onwards (and, as to the 25.12.2019 carve-out, from the initial act of 05/12/2019 onwards).

Caveat recorded deliberately: on EUR-Lex, the *consolidated* text is an informative document; the authoritative sources are the amending/repealing instruments as published (here Art. 9 of Regulation 2019/2015, OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68) together with M1 and M2 as published. The four independent renderings checked agree word for word, so no divergence risk arises on this provision.

## 4. Temporal-logic note (why the 25 December 2019 carve-out is not an anomaly)

EU drafting distinguishes three moments: **entry into force**, **date of application**, and **date of effect of a repeal**. Regulation 2019/2015 entered into force on 25 December 2019 but applied only from 1 September 2021. Article 9 deliberately splits the repeal of 874/2012:

- the **two excepted paragraphs** — Art. 3(2) and Art. 4(2) of 874/2012 — were repealed **with effect from 25 December 2019**, i.e. the day the repealing regulation itself entered into force, so those two obligations fell away immediately; and
- the **remainder** of 874/2012 stayed alive until **1 September 2021**, the date on which the new labelling regime began to apply, avoiding a regulatory gap between the old and new labelling rules.

That is why the request's "earlier on 25 December 2019" phrasing is correct and why the answer to ask 2 is not 25 December 2019: the general repeal date is 1 September 2021, and only the two named paragraphs fell on 25 December 2019.

## 5. Verification procedure (reproducible)

1. Open the ELI for the act: `https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2019/2015`. Read the "All consolidated versions" list and the "Amended by" table. Confirm the latest consolidation point on or before 21.11.2026 and confirm Article 9 carries no amendment marker.
2. Open Article 9 in that consolidation (here `…/reg_del/2019/2015/2023-09-30`) and copy the repeal sentence.
3. Cross-check against the original OJ act (`…/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=oj:JOL_2019_315_R_0003`) — the published version is the authoritative one.
4. Cross-check against CELEX 32019R2015 and, for retained/EU-derived domestic text, legislation.gov.uk `eur/2019/2015/article/9`.
5. Record for each check: URL, fetch timestamp, and the sentence as rendered. A discrepancy on any of the four is the kill trigger: stop and re-pin the version before answering.

answer:
# Seasonal space heating particulate matter emission limits — Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1189, text in force on 2026-11-21

## 1. Answer

| Boiler type | Seasonal space heating PM limit | Unit | Legal basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automatically stoked solid fuel boiler | **40** | mg/m³ | Annex II, point 1(c) |
| Manually stoked solid fuel boiler | **60** | mg/m³ | Annex II, point 1(c) |

Verbatim text of Annex II, point 1(c):

> "seasonal space heating emissions of particulate matter shall not be higher than 40 mg/m3 for automatically stoked boilers and not be higher than 60 mg/m3 for manually stoked boilers;"

These are the **mandatory ecodesign requirements**, not benchmarks. They apply to solid fuel boilers from **1 January 2020** (Article 3(2) with Annex II, point 1 chapeau: "From 1 January 2020 solid fuel boilers shall comply with the following requirements"), and they are unchanged and in force on 2026-11-21.

## 2. Version control — what "as in force on 2026-11-21" means here

- Base act: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1189 of 28 April 2015, OJ L 193, 21.7.2015, p. 100–114; CELEX 32015R1189; ELI http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/1189/oj.
- Entry into force: Article 9 — twentieth day following publication, i.e. 10 August 2015.
- Amendments: **one only** — Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/2282 of 30 November 2016 (OJ L 346, 20.12.2016, p. 51), shown in the consolidated text's amendment table as "►M1". The current consolidated version published on EUR-Lex is **02015R1189-20170109 (09/01/2017)**, and the EUR-Lex act page lists 09/01/2017 as the current consolidated version, with no later consolidated version offered.
- Effect of 2016/2282: it rewrote the conformity-assessment/verification provisions (Annex IV tolerances and related wording). It did **not** touch Annex II point 1(c). The consolidated text 02015R1189-20170109 still carries "40 mg/m3 … 60 mg/m3" verbatim, and so do the pre- and post-amendment renderings (CELEX 32015R1189; legislation.gov.uk versions 28/04/2015, 09/01/2017, 31/01/2020, 31/12/2020).
- Transitional provision: Article 8 allowed Member States to permit national-provision boilers until 1 January 2020. That window is closed; on 2026-11-21 the Annex II limits are the operative requirements.
- Article 7 review (report to the Consultation Forum by 1 January 2022) is a review obligation, not an amendment. No review-driven amendment appears in any retrieved version.
- Framework context (does not change the values): Regulation (EU) 2015/1189 implements Directive 2009/125/EC. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR) repeals Directive 2009/125/EC with effect from 18 July 2024, but existing implementing measures remain in force until expressly repealed or replaced by ESPR delegated acts. No repeal of 2015/1189 is recorded in the sources retrieved.

**Residual verification step (the one thing to re-do on the day of use):** open the EUR-Lex "All consolidated versions" list for CELEX 32015R1189 and confirm that 09/01/2017 is still the latest consolidated version and that no corrigendum/amendment has altered Annex II point 1(c). If a later consolidation exists, re-read point 1(c) before relying on 40/60.

## 3. What the 40 and 60 mg/m³ figures are measured against (metric and reference conditions)

A limit of "40 mg/m³" is meaningless without the metric, so the following is part of the answer:

- **Definition (Annex I, point 1)** — "seasonal space heating emissions" for PM is:
  - automatically stoked boilers: weighted average of emissions at rated heat output and at **30 %** of rated heat output;
  - manually stoked boilers **that can** be operated at 50 % of rated heat output in continuous mode: weighted average of emissions at rated heat output and at **50 %** of rated heat output;
  - manually stoked boilers **that cannot** be operated at 50 % or less of rated heat output in continuous mode: emissions at **rated heat output only**;
  - solid fuel cogeneration boilers: emissions at rated heat output only.
- **Calculation (Annex III, point 6(b))**:
  - manually stoked (50 % capable) and automatically stoked: `Es = 0,85 × Es,p + 0,15 × Es,n`
  - manually stoked (not 50 % capable) and cogeneration: `Es = Es,n`
  - where `Es,p` = emissions at 30 % or 50 % of rated heat output as applicable, `Es,n` = emissions at rated heat output.
- **Reference conditions (Annex III, point 6(a))**: emissions expressed standardised to a **dry flue gas basis at 10 % oxygen** and standard conditions at **0 °C and 1 013 mbar**.
- **Measurement method**: PM by a **gravimetric method excluding any particulate matter formed by organic gaseous compounds when flue gas is mixed with ambient air**.
- **Fuel coverage (Annex II, point 1, closing sentence)**: "These requirements shall be met for the preferred fuel and for any other suitable fuel for the solid fuel boiler."

## 4. Do not confuse three different sets of numbers in this regulation

| Category | PM figure | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ecodesign limit, automatically stoked | 40 mg/m³ | **Binding** | Annex II, point 1(c) |
| Ecodesign limit, manually stoked | 60 mg/m³ | **Binding** | Annex II, point 1(c) |
| Indicative BAT benchmark (biomass boilers) | 2 mg/m³ | Non-binding, indicative only | Annex V, point 2(a) |
| Indicative BAT benchmark (fossil fuel boilers) | 10 mg/m³ | Non-binding, indicative only | Annex V, point 2(a) |
| Verification tolerance (market surveillance) | determined value may not exceed the declared value by more than 9 mg/m³ | Tolerance, not a limit | Annex IV (as amended by (EU) 2016/2282) |

The Annex V benchmarks are "indicative benchmarks for the best available technology" and are explicitly framed as such; they are not compliance obligations and are not the answer to this question. The 9 mg/m³ figure is the maximum permitted deviation of a verification measurement from the declared value; it is not an emission limit and must not be added to 40/60 as if it were headroom.

## 5. Scope qualification

The limits apply to **solid fuel boilers with a rated heat output of 500 kW or less** placed on the market or put into service in the Union, including those integrated in packages as defined in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/1187 (Article 1(1)), subject to the exclusions in **Article 1(2)** (which the user should consult for edge cases such as non-solid-fuel appliances and appliances outside the rated-output band). Where a boiler falls outside Article 1, the 40/60 mg/m³ figures do not apply to it.

Note that Regulation (EU) 2015/1187 (energy labelling of solid fuel boilers and packages) is a separate instrument and does not set emission limits; it only requires the PM value to be declared in the label/product information.

## 6. Worked compliance checks (arithmetic verified)

**Case A — automatically stoked boiler.** Declared Es,n = 55 mg/m³, Es,p (at 30 %) = 35 mg/m³.
`Es = 0,85 × 35 + 0,15 × 55 = 29,75 + 8,25 = 38,0 mg/m³` → 38,0 ≤ 40 → **passes** the Annex II 1(c) limit.

**Case B — manually stoked boiler capable of 50 % continuous operation.** Declared Es,n = 55 mg/m³, Es,p (at 50 %) = 62 mg/m³.
`Es = 0,85 × 62 + 0,15 × 55 = 52,70 + 8,25 = 60,95 mg/m³` → 60,95 > 60 → **fails** the Annex II 1(c) limit (margin of 0,95 mg/m³).

**Case C — manually stoked boiler not capable of ≤50 % continuous operation.** Only Es,n is used: Es = Es,n. Declared Es,n = 58 mg/m³ → 58 ≤ 60 → **passes**. Declared Es,n = 61 mg/m³ → 61 > 60 → **fails**.

All three cases use exactly the limits stated in section 1 (40 auto / 60 manual) and the weighting of Annex III point 6(b); no case is decided against a different number.

## 7. One-line answer for a declaration or technical file

"Seasonal space heating particulate matter emissions, determined per Annex III of Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1189 and expressed on a dry flue gas basis at 10 % O₂, 0 °C and 1 013 mbar, do not exceed 40 mg/m³ (automatically stoked) / 60 mg/m³ (manually stoked), as required by Annex II, point 1(c), applicable from 1 January 2020 and in force on 2026-11-21."

SUBJECT: Repeal of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015, as in force on 2026-11-21.

1. VERSION PINNING (satisfies the constraint in ask 1)
   Instrument: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 with regard to energy labelling of light sources and repealing Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 (OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68; CELEX 32019R2015; ELI http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/2015/oj).
   Text consulted for the 2026-11-21 cut-off: the current EUR-Lex consolidation, CELEX 02019R2015-20230930, ELI http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/2015/2023-09-30, file 02019R2015 — EN — 30.09.2023 — 005.001.
   Amendment chain shown in the 'Amended by' table of that consolidation: ►B initial act; ►M1 Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/340 of 17 December 2020 (OJ L 68, 26.2.2021, p. 62); ►M2 Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2048 of 4 July 2023 (OJ L 236, 26.9.2023, p. 1). No third amending act appears. EUR-Lex lists 30/09/2023 as the latest consolidated version, so it is the text in force on 2026-11-21.
   Robustness: Article 9 is word-for-word identical in the initial act (OJ L 315), in the intermediate consolidation 02019R2015-20210701 and in the current consolidation 02019R2015-20230930. Neither M1 nor M2 touches Article 9 (M1 rewrote Article 10 and parts of the Annexes; M2 amended Annexes). The answer is therefore invariant across every consolidation in the chain and cannot be altered by the choice of 2026-11-21 as the reference date. Both repeal dates are in the past relative to 2026-11-21.

2. OPERATIVE PROVISION — ARTICLE 9 (verbatim, consolidation 30/09/2023)
   "Article 9 — Repeal
    Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, with the exception of paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 which are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019."
   Mechanism: the repeal is effected by Article 9 of Regulation 2019/2015 itself — not by a separate later act. No amending act has changed these dates.

3. ANSWER TO ASK 2 — DATE OF REPEAL OF DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) No 874/2012
   1 September 2021 (full repeal, subject only to the two carve-outs in paragraph 4 below, which had already been repealed on 25 December 2019).
   Cross-check: the EUR-Lex document-relationship table for CELEX 32019R2015 records 'Repeal — 32012R0874 — 01/09/2021' and, separately, 'Repeal — 32012R0874 — Partial repeal — 25/12/2019'. This is consistent with Article 9 and with the Article 10 application date ('It shall apply from 1 September 2021').

4. ANSWER TO ASK 3 — THE TWO PARAGRAPHS REPEALED EARLIER, ON 25 DECEMBER 2019
   (a) paragraph 2 of Article 3; and
   (b) paragraph 2 of Article 4
   — in each case of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 of 12 July 2012 (OJ L 258, 26.9.2012, p. 1), i.e. the Regulation being repealed by Article 9 of 2019/2015, not paragraphs of 2019/2015 itself. Read literally: 'Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed ... with the exception of paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 which are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019.'
   Cross-check: the same EUR-Lex relationship table records the 25/12/2019 entry as a 'Partial repeal' of 32012R0874, and 25/12/2019 is also the entry into force of 2019/2015 under Article 10 (twentieth day after publication on 5.12.2019; EUR-Lex 'Date of effect: 25/12/2019; Entry into force'). The early partial repeal therefore coincides with the entry into force of the repealing act.

5. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER TABLE
   | Ask | Answer |
   | 1 (constraint) | Version in force on 2026-11-21 = consolidation 02019R2015-20230930 (ELI .../2019/2015/2023-09-30), as amended by 2021/340 and 2023/2048; Article 9 unchanged. |
   | 2 | Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 repealed with effect from 1 September 2021 (Article 9, 2019/2015). |
   | 3 | Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012, repealed with effect from 25 December 2019. |

6. SCOPE NOTE
   This is a legal-source identification and dating exercise on the consolidated English text of Regulation 2019/2015. It states what the text says and when each repeal takes effect; it does not opine on the subject matter of Article 3(2) or Article 4(2) of 874/2012, which is not recited in Article 9 and would require reading the repealed act itself.
